items.stem: Normalising an SME's earnings before valuation typically involves:

options.text: Adjusting for an owner's above-market salary and one-off items
options.rationale: Correct: normalisation restores sustainable, transferable earnings.

options.text: Adding back all expenses to maximise the figure
options.rationale: Only non-recurring or owner-specific items are adjusted, not all expenses.

options.text: Using the single best year ever recorded
options.rationale: A cherry-picked peak year is not sustainable earnings.
Owner pay must be adjusted to a market rate, not ignored.

items.explanation: Correct: normalisation restores sustainable, transferable earnings.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which two adjustments are commonly applied when valuing a small, privately held business? (Select TWO)

options.text: A discount for lack of marketability
options.rationale: Correct: private stakes are harder to sell, warranting a discount.

options.text: A discount for a minority (non-controlling) interest
options.rationale: Correct: a minority stake lacks control and is often discounted.

options.text: A premium because it is unlisted
options.rationale: Being unlisted usually reduces, not raises, value.

options.text: Ignoring risk because it is a family firm
options.rationale: Family ownership does not remove risk.

items.explanation: Correct: private stakes are harder to sell, warranting a discount.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Applying a large listed company's valuation multiple directly to a tiny SME tends to:

options.rationale: Correct: small firms are riskier and less liquid, warranting lower multiples.
Large-company multiples are generally higher, overstating SME value.

options.text: Have no effect on the valuation
options.rationale: The multiple directly drives the result.

items.explanation: Correct: small firms are riskier and less liquid, warranting lower multiples.
